findings.title: Password recovery form reachable from an existing session, allowing a password change without the current password
findings.impact: Brief physical access to a signed-in browser becomes permanent account takeover. For a doctor account this yields clinical read/write and staff administration for the clinic; the legitimate owner is locked out.
findings.preconditions: Access to a browser tab holding a live session. No credentials or token theft required.
findings.root_cause: The recovery view was selected from location.pathname alone, and the project's secure-password-change (re-authentication) setting is not enabled.
findings.violated_invariant: A password change must be authorised by the current password or by a fresh recovery token.
findings.evidence: Pre-fix: useState(location.pathname === '/auth/recovery'); the form calls client.auth.updateUser({ password }) with no re-authentication.
findings.reproduction: Sign in, navigate to <origin>/auth/recovery in the same tab. Expected: workspace. Actual (pre-fix): 'Choose a new password' form, and submission succeeds.
findings.fix: The route now also requires a PKCE 'code' query parameter on the page load; the PASSWORD_RECOVERY event path is unchanged so genuine recovery links still work.
findings.residual_risk: Client-side control only. An attacker at the same keyboard can call updateUser from the console. On 2026-09-19 the project's 'Secure password change' setting was enabled, which requires reauthentication - but only for sessions older than 24 hours, so a workstation signed in that morning is still exposed. The control that would close this is 'Require current password when updating', deliberately left off because the recovery screen is this app's only password-update path and a recovering user cannot supply a current password. Test it against a real recovery once hosting exists; see OWNER-ACTIONS.md item 1.

findings.title: Default privileges granted every future object in schema public to anon and authenticated
findings.impact: Latent but broad: any table added by a future migration would have been readable and writable by every signed-in user of any clinic before a policy existed for it.
affected: pg_default_acl for role postgres in schema public (objtypes r, S, f)
findings.preconditions: None today; triggered by the next CREATE TABLE in public.
findings.root_cause: Supabase's permissive project default was never narrowed.
findings.violated_invariant: A new database object is inaccessible until a migration deliberately grants access.
findings.evidence: Pre-fix pg_default_acl for role postgres: {postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres,anon=arwdDxtm/postgres,authenticated=arwdDxtm/postgres,service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres}. Post-fix for role postgres: postgres and service_role only.
findings.reproduction: CREATE TABLE public.probe(id int); then has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.probe','select'). Expected false, actual (pre-fix) true.
findings.fix: Migration 20260918234315: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres IN SCHEMA public REVOKE ALL ON TABLES/SEQUENCES FROM anon, authenticated and REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTIONS FROM public, anon, authenticated; equivalent revoke for clinic_private functions.
findings.residual_risk: Partially closed. Re-checked 2026-09-19 13:02 UTC: a second set of default ACLs in public is owned by the platform role supabase_admin and still grants anon and authenticated on future tables, sequences and functions. ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE supabase_admin is refused because postgres is not a member of that role, so the project owner cannot change it from SQL. Migrations, the MCP connection and the dashboard SQL editor all create objects as postgres and are covered; the gap applies only to objects the Supabase platform itself creates in public. Future migrations must still grant access explicitly, and any new public object should be checked with has_table_privilege rather than assumed private. An earlier version of this entry implied the fix covered the whole schema; this corrects it.

findings.title: Complete clinical documents readable through audit_events payload columns
findings.impact: An administrator's token could retrieve full before/after visit documents (notes, diagnoses, prescriptions) from an immutable, never-purged table with a single query string, bypassing the narrow column list both clients use.
findings.preconditions: Active is_admin doctor membership and its JWT. Same clinic only; not cross-tenant.
findings.root_cause: Field-level authorization was implemented in two clients rather than in the database.
findings.violated_invariant: Clinical content is reachable only through the clinical read path governed by the clinical_read capability.
findings.evidence: AUD-02: GET /rest/v1/audit_events?select=new_value now returns 403/42501; AUD-03 select=* likewise; AUD-01 metadata columns still return rows; AUD-04 assistants still see none.
findings.reproduction: As an is_admin doctor: GET /rest/v1/audit_events?select=new_value&clinic_id=eq.<clinic>. Expected 42501, actual (pre-fix) rows containing clinical text.
findings.fix: Migration 20260918234315: REVOKE SELECT ON public.audit_events FROM authenticated, then GRANT SELECT on the eight metadata columns only. No client change required.
findings.residual_risk: Payload columns still exist and accumulate. Storing a diff or relocating payloads to clinic_private, plus a retention policy, remains open.

findings.title: Document file name extension not bound to the verified content type; finalize did not check stored MIME
findings.impact: A genuine PDF could be stored as report.html or scan.svg. Bytes are verified on download by both clients, so this is not in-origin execution; the risk is a colleague saving the file and the operating system trusting the extension.
findings.preconditions: Any clinic member permitted to upload.
findings.root_cause: File name and content type were validated independently and never compared; finalize compared only the stored object's size.
findings.violated_invariant: A document's name, its recorded type and its stored bytes must agree.
findings.evidence: DOC-02: staging a PNG named .html now returns ATTACHMENT_EXTENSION. PGlite: a stored object whose mimetype differs from the record returns ATTACHMENT_TYPE_MISMATCH.
findings.reproduction: clinic_begin_attachment(p_file_name := 'report.html', p_content_type := 'application/pdf'). Expected rejection, actual (pre-fix) accepted.
findings.fix: Server: begin_attachment rejects a mismatched present extension (absent extension still allowed); finalize_attachment compares metadata->>'mimetype'. Client: extensionMatches() refuses the upload; downloadName() saves under an extension matching the detected type and sanitises path-hostile characters.
findings.residual_risk: Content itself is still verified only by clients until CW-11 is addressed.

findings.title: clinic_private implementations executable by authenticated, bypassing wrapper-level presence and freshness checks
findings.impact: Calling an implementation directly would skip logic that lives only in the public wrapper - for clinic_apply_command that is the send action's _expires_at freshness check and require_doctor_presence(). Not reachable over HTTP, so defence-in-depth rather than a demonstrated bypass.
findings.preconditions: Would require a direct database connection as the authenticated role, or exposing clinic_private through PostgREST. Neither is possible today.
findings.root_cause: The public wrappers were SECURITY INVOKER, which required EXECUTE grants on the implementations.
findings.violated_invariant: Authorization and workflow gates are enforced at a layer the consumer cannot route around.
findings.evidence: PRIV-09: POST /rest/v1/rpc/apply_command with Content-Profile: clinic_private returns 406 PGRST106 'Only the following schemas are exposed: public, graphql_public'. Post-fix catalog: only allowed and attachment_object_allowed executable by authenticated.
findings.fix: Migration 20260918234315: 15 public wrappers become SECURITY DEFINER with search_path=''; clinic_search_patients deliberately stays SECURITY INVOKER so RLS filters its rows; EXECUTE on clinic_private revoked from public, anon and authenticated except the two RLS helpers.
findings.residual_risk: The Supabase advisor now reports lint 0029 for the 15 definer wrappers. That is the intended API surface; each implementation re-checks auth.uid() and membership.

findings.title: Web password policy (8 characters) weaker than the mobile apps (12-72) on the same accounts
findings.impact: The weaker of two policies governed shared accounts, lowering resistance to guessing and credential stuffing for accounts that hold clinical data.
findings.root_cause: The web client set its own minLength without reference to the mobile policy or a server-side minimum.
findings.violated_invariant: One account has one password policy, enforced at its strongest across all clients.
findings.evidence: Pre-fix minLength={mode === 'signup' ? 8 : 1} and minLength={8} on both recovery fields.
findings.reproduction: Create an account through the web UI with an 8-character password. Expected rejection, actual (pre-fix) accepted.
findings.fix: minLength={12} maxLength={72} on sign-up, new password and confirmation fields.
findings.residual_risk: A client-side minimum is advisory. The project's minimum-length setting and leaked-password protection are the enforcing controls (CW-12).

findings.regression_test: Covered indirectly by the browser suite; the enforcing control is server-side and listed as an owner action.

findings.title: Unbounded clinics per user and unbounded presence rows per doctor
findings.impact: One account could create clinics indefinitely, each seeding rows in clinics, clinic_memberships, audit_events and patient_counters; a doctor token could grow doctor_device_presence without limit. Storage and index growth on a shared backend; no tenant boundary crossed.
findings.preconditions: Any signed-in user with a confirmed e-mail (clinics); any active doctor (presence).
findings.violated_invariant: A single account cannot consume unbounded shared resources.
findings.evidence: PGlite: the 21st clinic_create now raises CLINIC_LIMIT; after 14 heartbeats with distinct device ids, exactly 10 presence rows remain.
findings.reproduction: Call clinic_create 21 times. Expected CLINIC_LIMIT, actual (pre-fix) 21 clinics.
findings.fix: Migration 20260918234315: 20-clinic cap under a per-user advisory lock (so concurrent calls cannot race past it); presence capped at 10 rows per doctor, never evicting a row cited by an immutable receipt.
findings.residual_risk: Clinic creation is still open to any confirmed account; rate limiting of sign-up remains a project setting.

findings.title: patients.mobile bounded by digit count but not by raw length
findings.impact: A value could carry unbounded punctuation around 7-20 valid digits. That text is copied twice into audit_events per save and broadcast to every clinic member over Realtime.
findings.preconditions: Any clinic member who can save a patient.
findings.root_cause: The existing check stripped non-digits before measuring length.
findings.violated_invariant: Every client-supplied text column has an explicit maximum length at the table.
findings.evidence: Live data unaffected: longest existing value 13 characters, zero values containing non-digits.
findings.reproduction: Save a patient with mobile = 41 punctuation characters plus a valid number. Expected 23514, actual (pre-fix) accepted.
findings.fix: Migration 20260918234315: constraint patients_mobile_bound check (length(mobile) <= 40), matching the client maxLength.

findings.title: CI actions referenced by mutable version tags
findings.impact: A tag can be moved, so a compromise of the referenced action repositories would execute attacker-controlled code in a workflow that runs on pull_request. Blast radius is small: permissions contents: read, no secrets, no deployment.
findings.preconditions: Compromise or retagging of actions/checkout, actions/setup-node or actions/upload-artifact.
findings.root_cause: Tag references rather than commit pinning.
findings.violated_invariant: Build inputs are immutable and verifiable.
findings.evidence: Pre-fix: uses: actions/checkout@v7. Post-fix: uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
findings.reproduction: Static review of the workflow file.
findings.fix: All three actions pinned to the commit SHAs that v7 resolved to on 2026-09-19, with the tag kept as a trailing comment.
findings.residual_risk: Pins must be refreshed deliberately; a dependency-update policy for actions is recommended.

findings.title: Built document carried no Content Security Policy
findings.impact: A host that sends no headers would serve the application with no policy at all. The nginx file is an example and no deployment exists to verify.
findings.preconditions: Requires an injection foothold to exploit; the policy is a mitigation layer.
findings.root_cause: The policy existed only in an example server configuration that nothing consumes.
findings.violated_invariant: The application ships with its own baseline defences rather than depending on unverified hosting.
findings.evidence: dist/index.html now contains meta http-equiv=Content-Security-Policy with default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; connect-src limited to the Supabase origins.
findings.fix: A build-only Vite plugin injects the baseline policy as a meta tag.
findings.residual_risk: frame-ancestors and Strict-Transport-Security cannot be set by a meta tag; the nginx headers remain mandatory and are now called out in the README.

findings.title: Document digest and bytes are verified only by clients
findings.impact: A member controlling both the file and its declared digest can store an object other members cannot open, or one matching its declared type only at the header. A hash recorded by the party supplying the file detects transport corruption, not a hostile uploader.
findings.preconditions: Any clinic member permitted to upload.
findings.root_cause: No server-side component reads the stored bytes; the system has no server code at all.
findings.violated_invariant: Stored clinical documents are verifiably the bytes the record describes.
findings.evidence: finalize_attachment compares metadata size and (since this audit) mimetype only; sha256 is never recomputed server-side.
findings.reproduction: Stage an attachment with a sha256 that does not match the bytes, upload, finalize. Expected rejection, actual: state becomes ready and other members' clients refuse the download on hash mismatch.
findings.fix: Proposal only: proposed-fixes/proposed-verify-attachment-edge-function.md - an Edge Function with the service role downloads the object, verifies length, digest and magic bytes, then marks the attachment ready.
findings.residual_risk: Unmitigated beyond the 20 MiB / four-MIME bucket, the CW-04 extension binding and client-side magic-byte checks.

findings.title: Leaked-password protection disabled and no second factor on clinical accounts
findings.impact: A doctor account taken over by credential stuffing yields full clinical read/write and staff administration for its clinic, and the same credentials work in the mobile apps.
findings.preconditions: Remote attacker with a candidate credential list. Sign-up is open, so the login surface is public.
findings.root_cause: Project settings were never hardened; MFA was never introduced.
findings.violated_invariant: Accounts holding clinical data resist credential reuse and single-factor compromise.
findings.evidence: Supabase security advisor WARN auth_leaked_password_protection, present both before and after this engagement. /auth/v1/settings shows email-only providers, disable_signup=false, no passkeys.
findings.reproduction: Read the security advisor for the project.
findings.fix: Partly applied 2026-09-19. Minimum password length raised from 6 to 12 and verified server-side (an 11-character sign-up returns weak_password). Leaked-password protection could NOT be enabled: it requires a Supabase Pro plan and the Homeversion org is on Free; the save was rejected with 'Configuring leaked password protection via HaveIBeenPwned.org is available on Pro Plans and up.' Remaining owner actions: upgrade the plan then enable it; consider TOTP MFA for doctors and then require aal2 for the admin and clinical_write capabilities in clinic_private.allowed.
findings.residual_risk: Leaked-password protection is blocked by plan tier, so the auth_leaked_password_protection advisor warning persists and is a billing decision, not a technical one. Until then the 12-character minimum plus the client rule is the whole password defence, which raises the value of MFA for doctor accounts.

findings.title: Clinical writes do not require the handoff receipt server-side
findings.impact: Attribution strength rather than access control: the actor is already the assigned doctor of a withDoctor appointment. The invariant that clinical notes belong to a doctor who confirmed receipt of that specific handoff lives in the clients only.
findings.preconditions: Assigned doctor of an appointment in status withDoctor.
findings.root_cause: The receipt model was added for delivery confirmation and never made a precondition of clinical writes.
findings.violated_invariant: Clinical notes are attributable to a doctor who acknowledged this handoff version.
findings.evidence: apply_command requires appointment status withDoctor and doctor_id = auth.uid(), with no appointment_receipts lookup.
findings.reproduction: As the assigned doctor, send a visit save without calling clinic_acknowledge_appointment. Expected RECEIPT_REQUIRED under the proposal; actual: accepted.
findings.residual_risk: Unchanged until applied; requires mobile team agreement because it changes offline outbox ordering.

findings.title: Sign-out revokes only the local session
findings.impact: A refresh token captured before sign-out remains usable until expiry. The token is removed from sessionStorage, so exploitation requires prior exfiltration.
findings.root_cause: scope: 'local' is used to avoid signing the user out of the mobile apps, which share the account.
findings.violated_invariant: Sign-out ends the session everywhere it can be replayed.
findings.evidence: await client.auth.signOut({ scope: 'local' }); the password-recovery path correctly uses scope: 'global'.
findings.fix: Not changed. Changing it silently would sign users out of their phones. Recommended instead: shorten refresh-token lifetime, or offer an explicit 'sign out everywhere' action.
findings.residual_risk: Accepted trade-off, documented for the owner to decide.

findings.title: Realtime delivers full patient rows to every clinic member
findings.impact: None additional: recipients can already read the same demographics through PostgREST. visits events are filtered per subscriber by RLS, which is the part that matters.
findings.root_cause: postgres_changes carries full row payloads by design.
findings.evidence: Publication contains appointments, patients, visits with insert/update/delete.

findings.title: Distinct error codes reveal that a UUID exists in another clinic
findings.impact: An attacker already holding a valid UUID learns it exists somewhere in the system. UUIDv4 is not enumerable and the row's contents stay unreachable.
findings.root_cause: Precise error codes aid legitimate clients.
findings.evidence: XC-09 returns CROSS_CLINIC_ID where an unknown id returns a different error.

findings.title: Storage objects can never be deleted by clients; orphans accumulate
findings.impact: Retention is intentional, but failed uploads and orphaned objects accumulate with no sweeper and no client or SQL deletion path.
findings.root_cause: No DELETE policy by design; SQL deletion blocked by Supabase.
findings.evidence: DOC-09: uploader deletion refused. This audit produced exactly one orphan, recorded in TEST-RESULTS.md section 6.
findings.fix: The audit's orphan was deleted through the dashboard on 2026-09-19: the 70-byte object, then its empty folder and Supabase's zero-byte .emptyFolderPlaceholder. Verified in storage.objects: clinic-documents now holds exactly one object, the real 4.4 MB attachment, and it is referenced by an attachments row. The general gap is unchanged: clients still have no DELETE policy and failed uploads would still accumulate, so a scheduled sweeper remains worth considering.
findings.residual_risk: Growth over time from failed uploads; no sweeper exists. No orphan is present today.

findings.title: Deployment security entirely unverified (no deployment exists)
findings.impact: Headers, TLS, HSTS, caching of clinical responses, SPA fallback for /auth/recovery and origin isolation of the document preview are untested and could each undermine controls verified elsewhere.
findings.root_cause: No public deployment is included, confirmed by repository review.
findings.violated_invariant: n/a - coverage gap, recorded rather than assumed safe.
findings.evidence: No hosting artefacts, no domain, no TLS material in the repository.
findings.fix: Deploy behind the nginx configuration, then verify headers, TLS, HSTS, cache-control on clinical responses, SPA fallback and preview isolation against the live origin.
